speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; these are urgent symptoms that require immediate clarification. To start our assessment, please tell me your exact age in hours or days and whether you have passed meconium yet.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus.

This is a life-threatening emergency in a newborn with bilious vomiting. Although the family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, the presence of bilious vomiting at six hours of life makes intestinal malrotation with volvulus the most critical and likely diagnosis that must be ruled out immediately.
